title: Facilitating Transition to SimplyGo Fare Platform
what_it_is: Facilitating Transition to SimplyGo Fare Platform

sections.label: Questions on card ticketing costs
sections.summary: MPs asked the Minister for Transport about the $40 million cost, shelf life, operational lifespan and whether spending on the card-based ticketing system is one-off or recurring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) why is there a need to spend an additional $40 million so that commuters can continue to use the present EZ-Link card-based ticketing system; and (b) what is the estimated shelf life of this proposed upgraded solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport what is the operational lifespan of the extended card-based ticketing system that was announced by the Land Transport Authority on 22 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the cost of $40 million to renew the present card-based ticketing system and continuing to run it alongside the SimplyGo system is a one-off or recurring expenditure; (b) how much has been spent or committed to be spent in (i) the development of the SimplyGo system and (ii) this conversion attempt, including time, manpower and other expenses.

sections.label: Questions on SimplyGo expenditure and savings
sections.summary: MPs asked about total government expenditure on SimplyGo, LTA's projected annual savings from using only SimplyGo, and whether savings would be passed to commuters as fare rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the total government expenditure to-date in developing the SimplyGo system for public transport; (b) what are LTA’s projected annual savings from the use of only the SimplyGo system on public transport as compared to the current simultaneous use of both SimplyGo and card-based ticketing (CBT) systems; and (c) whether LTA plans to pass these cost savings on to commuters in the form of fare rebates when the CBT systems are eventually decommissioned.

sections.label: SimplyGo adoption among adult commuters
sections.summary: In December 2023, 64% of adult commuters used the SimplyGo ABT system, and about 9,000 converted their CBT cards from 23 to 31 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In December 2023, 41% of adult commuters were using bank cards and mobile wallets for public transport, while another 23% of adult commuters were using SimplyGo ABT stored value cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In total, 64% or about two-thirds of adult commuters were using the SimplyGo ABT system in December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The proportion of adult commuters using SimplyGo has continued to increase after our announcement on 22 January 2024, when the public was informed that LTA would extend the CBT system for adult commuters till at least 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: From 23 to 31 January 2024, about 9,000 adult commuters, or around 1,000 per day, have converted their CBT cards to the SimplyGo system.

sections.label: Cost of extending CBT system
sections.summary: LTA would need to spend an estimated $40 million to buy new hardware and equipment and operate and maintain the system until at least 2030.

sentences.text: To extend the system until at least 2030, LTA would need to spend an estimated $40 million to buy new hardware and equipment, and then operate and maintain the system over the next few years.

sections.label: Decision not to sunset CBT
sections.summary: After commuter feedback, the decision to sunset the CBT system for adult commuters was not proceeded with, so commuters can still use CBT EZ-Link or NETS FlashPay cards.

sentences.text: After listening to the feedback from commuters, we understand their concerns and respect their preferences.

We therefore decided not to proceed with the earlier decision to sunset the CBT system for adult commuters, so that commuters who prefer to have the option of using CBT EZ-Link cards or NETS FlashPay cards to pay for public transport can still do so.

sections.label: Government bears $40 million cost
sections.summary: The estimated $40 million to maintain the adult CBT system until at least 2030 will be borne by the Government and will not affect public transport fares.

sentences.text: In making this decision, we will not be able to avoid the estimated cost of $40 million to maintain the adult CBT system till at least 2030.
The estimated cost of $40 million will be borne by the Government and will not affect public transport fares.

sections.label: Decision factors and public funds
sections.summary: The decision will consider technical limitations, commuter preference, consultation, costs and benefits, with MOT and LTA spending public funds prudently.

sentences.text: In making the decision subsequently, important factors would include whether we can overcome the current technical limitations of the ABT system and which system commuters prefer to use.
We will consult widely to understand the needs of different groups of commuters and carefully assess the costs and benefits.
In planning and implementing our next steps, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and LTA will continue to spend public funds prudently.
In areas where we can save money, we will try to reduce costs as much as possible.
But where it is necessary to spend, we will do so.

sections.label: Cost of CBT system
sections.summary: This is the estimated cost to purchase hardware and software and to operate and maintain the CBT system for adult commuters till at least 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And if so, why was it not announced publicly at that point in time?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is the estimated cost to purchase new hardware and equipment, software and also to operate and maintain the CBT system for adult commuters till at least 2030.

sections.label: Avoiding extension and commuter preference
sections.summary: The aim was to avoid extending the system at end-of-life in 2024, but LTA under-estimated commuters' strong preference to see fare deductions and card balances.

sentences.text: It is really to try and avoid incurring the cost of extending the system when it reaches end-of-life in 2024.
And also, LTA observed that by December 2023, about two-thirds of adult commuters have switched over to using SimplyGo, whether bank cards, mobile wallets, or the SimplyGo stored value ABT cards.
But we had under-estimated the strong preference of commuters who would like to continue seeing the fare deductions and the card balances at the fare gates and at the bus card readers.

sections.label: Expiring stored value cards
sections.summary: When current stored value cards expire, issuing new cards under the integrated system could allow gradual progress towards one CBT system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But as Members are aware, these stored value cards, EZ-Link cards, for example, have an expiry date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, when the current cards expire, if we are able to then issue a new card under the integrated system, then in the future, we can gradually and progressively work towards having one CBT system.

sections.label: ABT display limitations
sections.summary: ABT systems currently cannot quickly display fare deductions and card balances at fare gates and bus card readers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: At the moment, ABT systems are still unable to display fare deductions and card balances at the fare gates and at the bus card readers quickly.

sections.label: Latency and upgrading SimplyGo
sections.summary: The Minister is asked the latency preventing fare balance display and whether LTA could use $40 million to upgrade SimplyGo instead of extending the card-based system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, can the Minister share exactly what is the latency, preferably in milliseconds, that prevents the fare balance from being shown at the gate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, instead of spending $40 million to extend the life of the card-based ticketing system for another six years, can LTA instead use that money to upgrade the SimplyGo system to overcome these technical constraints?

sections.label: Tap out balance and card blocking
sections.summary: LTA would let the person tap out, compute balances at the backend with a short delay, and block the card on the next tap-in if balance is insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: LTA would let the person tap out and then compute the balances at the backend and that will then be reflected on the app, as Mr Giam mentioned, with a short delay; not immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But the next time when the user taps in and assuming that user does not have sufficient balance after the last journey, this card will then be blocked.

sections.label: SimplyGo expansion and CBT extension
sections.summary: LTA wants SimplyGo to be usable for retail, public transport and motoring, and plans to extend the adult CBT system until at least 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So that over time, just like today, your EZ-Link card can be used for retail, can be used for motoring and can be used for public transport, we also want to work towards SimplyGo being able to be used for all three – retail, public transport and also monitoring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But the process will take some time and that is why we need to extend the CBT system for adult commuters at this point in time because the system is reaching end-of-life in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We could, of course, extend by one year, as Mr Giam suggested, but I am not very confident that we will be able to find a solution in one year and having put in the hardware and the necessary equipment, we thought it is more prudent to plan, for the purposes of budgeting and planning, for it to run for at least a few years until at least 2030.

sections.label: Retaining CBT for concession cardholders
sections.summary: Based on feedback, especially from seniors unfamiliar with the app, LTA decided not to sunset the CBT system for concession cardholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In fact, that was one of the first feedback that came to LTA, especially from seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And based on that feedback, LTA then decided not to proceed with the plan to sunset the CBT system for concession cardholders because we understand that, for seniors, many of them told us that they are not familiar with using the app, so, that is why we decided to retain the CBT system for concession cardholders.

sections.label: Universal card and ERP 2.0 compatibility
sections.summary: The question asks whether SimplyGo enhancement plans include a universal card for public transport, retail and motoring, and whether it is compatible with the ERP 2.0 onboard unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The second question is actually on my Parliamentary Question No 19, that is, whether the plans to enhance the SimplyGo system include plans for a universal card which allows one to use it for public transport, retail, motoring, just as what the current EZ-Link and Flashpay cards can do and, importantly, whether it is compatible with the new onboard unit for ERP 2.0?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I had answered Mr Giam earlier on a similar point, that, over time, we do want to work towards having the SimplyGo card being able to be used for retail, public transport and also motoring.

sections.label: Seniors consulted on concession card CBT
sections.summary: Seniors were consulted early and, based on their feedback, LTA decided not to sunset the concession cards' CBT system as some may find switching difficult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Seniors were an important stakeholder group that we consulted early on and, based on their feedback, LTA then decided not to sunset the concession cards' CBT system because we are mindful that some of the senior commuters may find it difficult to make the switch because they may not be so familiar in using the app.
